A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Sparse Expansion and Neuronal Disentanglement and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendix A.1–A.8. Text and rendered-page comparisons reveal no material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original Pythia and Llama 2 compression experiments, neuronal analyses, and inference-latency measurements in Sections 3–5, Tables 1–2, and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark tables and appendix studies of expert counts and neuronal output distributions.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Algorithms 1–2 retain the same PCA reduction, K-means clustering and routing, cluster-specific SparseGPT pruning, and separate routing for down projections.

E1.justification: WikiText-2 calibration and evaluation coverage remains unchanged. Neither version adds or removes datasets, tasks, or test scenarios relative to the other.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods, including magnitude pruning, Wanda, SparseGPT, and dense references in Figure 7 and Table 1. Comparator membership elsewhere is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Both versions report identical Pythia and Llama 2 configurations, 16-cluster benchmarks, sparsity and quantization settings, evaluation metrics, and single-batch layer-latency procedures.

E4.justification: The high-Wasserstein-distance versus random-neuron compression study, expert-count sensitivity study, and appendix distribution and predictor analyses are all retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged, including the one-standard-error bars specified in Figure A.6 and boxplot conventions in Figure A.4. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting information is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and all main-text and appendix plots retain their results. For example, Table 1 retains 5.5839 for 50%-sparse, 16-bit Sparse Expansion on Llama 2 7B, and Table 2 retains the maximum 4.8x layer speedup.

T1.justification: The Hessian expression in Section 2, normalized Wasserstein-distance definition in Equation 1, and relative-improvement definition in Section 4 are unchanged. No mathematical result or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same scientific claims about one-shot sparsification efficiency, disentanglement through sparse experts, and Wasserstein distance as an indicator of neuronal entanglement.

C2.justification: Mechanism interpretations and applicability qualifications remain unchanged, including Section 7's limitation to per-layer timing and its proposed future end-to-end inference integration.

D1.justification: v2 adds an abstract statement that Sparse Expansion code is available and supplies the Shavit-Lab/Sparse-Expansion GitHub address. v1 lacks this access information for the proposed method; pseudocode, hardware, and other implementation disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 33 references and substantive positioning relative to sparsification, mixture-of-experts methods, and disentanglement remain in both versions.

P1.justification: The abstract gains the code-access sentence, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Remaining wording and section organization are unchanged apart from text reflow.

P2.justification: The abstract addition causes small layout shifts across pages 1–4, including the positions of Figures 1–2. Figure and table contents and captions are unchanged; pages 5–21 render identically.

improvement.justification: The new abstract-level repository address provides a concrete route to the implementation that v1 lacked, modestly improving reproducibility information. Scientific evidence, analyses, and limitations remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information but do not establish the repository's completeness or usability.
